summary: A callout pointing at one thing on the page, to say what it is or what changed — anchored to its target by id or ref, which is ringed while it shows. Several in a row are a Tour.
useWhen: someone asked what a control does, or what changed — a "What's new?" link beside a feature that moved
the explanation is about one place on the page and reads best beside it
it is one of several: then it is a Tour, which sequences them

useInstead.when: telling people something changed without their asking
useInstead.why: a coachmark takes focus; opened on page load, it pulls a keyboard or screen-reader user out of what they came to do

useInstead.when: several places in order — a first look round a page
useInstead.why: Tour gives the count, Back and Next, and one focus hand-back at the end; a row of separate coachmarks gives none of them

useInstead.when: a short hint on a control, on hover or focus
useInstead.why: a tooltip holds no controls and never takes focus; a coachmark is for what needs reading

useInstead.when: more detail the reader opens themselves from a control
useInstead.why: a toggletip is the control's own explanation; a coachmark points at the page from outside it

composition.note: `target` is an element id, or a ref. Render it when a person asks — `isOpen` from a button's press — with `onClose`, which gives it a close button and Escape. `footer` holds its actions and `progress` a count, which is how Tour builds its steps.
composition.example: <Coachmark target="export-runs" title="Export is here now" isOpen={open} onClose={() => setOpen(false)}>Runs export as CSV from this button, filtered as the table is.</Coachmark>

children.note: what to know about the target; linked as the dialog's description, so keep it to a sentence or two

footer.note: actions, end-aligned; one primary at most

requires: open it from a person's action, never on page load: it takes focus
guarantees: a dialog named by `title` and described by the body, focused when it appears so it is read out
not modal: the rest of the page is neither hidden from assistive tech nor inert, and focus is not trapped
Escape and the close button call `onClose`; focus goes back to where it was when it opened
its target is scrolled into view and ringed in border/primary-strong while it shows, and the ring goes when it closes
`placement` is logical: `start` is the right in a right-to-left page; React Aria flips it when there is no room, and the arrow follows the side it resolved to
a target that is not on the page shows nothing, rather than a callout pointing at nothing
a target drawn in the same commit as the coachmark — a section one press reveals and points at — is looked for again once it is on the page, and the coachmark still appears focused
in forced colours the target's ring is Highlight and the panel keeps a CanvasText edge
notes: No `onClose`, no close button, and Escape does nothing: give one unless something else closes it.
The close button is named by `closeLabel`, "Close" by default.

antiPatterns.dont: a Coachmark with `isOpen` true on page load
antiPatterns.do: a "What's new?" button that opens it, or a Banner
antiPatterns.why: it takes focus when it appears; unasked, it moves a keyboard user away from what they came to do

antiPatterns.dont: three Coachmarks opened one after another from your own state
antiPatterns.why: the count, Back, Next, the skipping of missing targets and the single focus hand-back are Tour's
a coachmark points at the page; a task needs its own surface
